data.why: No file upload exists; the scientist searches a gene symbol or RefSeq accession, and the engine answers from engine/data/cache (seeded for GAPDH, TP53, ACTB, EGFR, BRCA1, KRAS, MYC and ~60 other common genes across six species). The Custom sequence mode also ships a built-in GAPDH example (web/src/lib/__fixtures__/gapdh_custom.json) loadable in the UI, so nothing needs to be written or copied into prep/data.

goals: look up a gene (e.g. GAPDH, TP53) and see every curated RefSeq NM/NR transcript variant, folded so identical-sequence accessions aren't double-counted
pick a transcript variant and get the amplifiability verdict: a conventional unique-exon primer pair, an exon-exon-junction (EEJ) primer, or 'infeasible'
for an EEJ-dependent transcript, design a Tm-guided junction primer and drag-select alternate windows to see Tm/QC update live
design a single all-variant ('whole-transcript') primer pair that amplifies as many isoforms of a gene as possible, for a total-expression assay
paste custom transcripts with exon boundaries (no RefSeq record) to compare an arbitrary set of isoforms and design primers against a chosen target
check a candidate oligo's hairpin/self-dimer Tm and GC/length QC against the same thresholds the engine's designer uses

review.summary: The tree follows TransPrimer's stated purpose closely: classify a transcript variant as EEJ-independent, EEJ-dependent or infeasible, design a conventional or Tm-guided junction primer, or design one all-variant pair, all with database and custom input. The 11 screens sampled all support their nodes. It needs small structural fixes (t14 placement, a thin QC/Method phase), a few missing tasks and features, and a re-replay of the custom-mode tasks that weren't confirmed before filing.
